title_en: Extradition Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of ensuring the normal progress of extradition, strengthening international cooperation in penalizing crime, protecting the lawful rights and interests of individuals and organizations, and safeguarding national interests and social order.
Article 2 Extradition between the People's Republic of China and foreign countries shall be carried out in accordance with this Law.

Article 3 The People's Republic of China and foreign countries shall conduct extradition cooperation on the basis of equality and mutual benefit.
Extradition cooperation shall not impair the sovereignty, security and social public interests of the People's Republic of China.

Article 4 Extradition between the People's Republic of China and foreign countries shall be contacted through diplomatic channels. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China shall be the designated liaison authority for extradition.
If there are special provisions in the extradition treaty regarding the liaison authority, the provisions of the treaty shall be followed.

Article 5 In handling extradition cases, compulsory measures of extradition detention, extradition arrest or extradition residential surveillance may be taken against the person sought for extradition, depending on the circumstances.

Article 7 An extradition request made by a foreign state to the People's Republic of China must meet the following conditions at the same time before extradition may be granted:
(1) the act for which extradition is requested constitutes a crime under the laws of both the People's Republic of China and the requesting state;
(2) if the extradition request is made for the purpose of initiating criminal proceedings, the crime for which extradition is requested is punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of not less than one year or a heavier penalty under the laws of both the People's Republic of China and the requesting state; if the extradition request is made for the purpose of executing a penalty, the person sought has not yet served the remainder of the sentence of at least six months at the time the extradition request is made.
Where multiple crimes in the extradition request meet the condition specified in Item (1) of the preceding paragraph, extradition may be granted for all such crimes as long as one of them meets the condition specified in Item (2) of the preceding paragraph.
Article 10 An extradition request of a requesting state shall be submitted to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China.

Article 12 A requesting state requesting extradition shall, at the same time as issuing the written request, provide the following materials:
(1) if extradition is requested for the purpose of initiating criminal proceedings, a copy of an arrest warrant or other document having equivalent effect shall be attached; if extradition is requested for the purpose of executing a penalty, a copy of a legally effective judgment or order shall be attached, and if part of the penalty has already been executed, a certificate of the executed term of the penalty shall also be attached;
(2) necessary evidence or evidentiary materials of the crime.
If the requesting state possesses photographs, fingerprints or other materials that may be used to identify the person sought, it shall provide them.

Article 13 The extradition request or other relevant documents submitted by a requesting state under this Section shall be formally signed or sealed by the competent authority of the requesting state, and shall be accompanied by a Chinese translation or a translation in another language approved by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China.
Article 15 In the absence of an extradition treaty, the requesting state shall make a commitment of reciprocity.

Article 16 After receiving the extradition request from a requesting state, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall examine whether the extradition request and the attached documents and materials comply with the provisions of Section 2, Chapter II of this Law and the extradition treaty.
The Higher People's Court designated by the Supreme People's Court shall examine whether the extradition request made by the requesting state complies with the provisions of this Law and the extradition treaty regarding extradition conditions and shall render a ruling. The Supreme People's Court shall review the ruling made by the Higher People's Court.

Article 17 Where two or more states request the extradition of the same person for the same act or for different acts, the priority of accepting the extradition requests shall be determined by comprehensively considering factors such as the order in which the People's Republic of China received the extradition requests and whether there is an extradition treaty relationship between the People's Republic of China and the requesting states.

Article 18 Where the Ministry of Foreign Affairs examines the extradition request made by a requesting state and considers that it does not comply with the provisions of Section 2, Chapter II of this Law and the extradition treaty, it may request the requesting state to provide supplementary materials within thirty days. Upon the request of the requesting state, the aforesaid time limit may be extended by fifteen days.
If the requesting state fails to provide supplementary materials within the aforesaid time limit, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall terminate the extradition case. The requesting state may make a new request for extradition of the person for the same crime.

Article 19 Where the Ministry of Foreign Affairs examines the extradition request made by a requesting state and considers that it complies with the provisions of Section 2, Chapter II of this Law and the extradition treaty, it shall transfer the extradition request and the attached documents and materials to the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate.

Article 20 If the person sought has been placed under extradition detention before the foreign state makes a formal extradition request, the Supreme People's Court shall, upon receiving the extradition request and the attached documents and materials, promptly transfer them to the relevant Higher People's Court for examination.
If the person sought has not been placed under extradition detention before the foreign state makes a formal extradition request, the Supreme People's Court shall, upon receiving the extradition request and the attached documents and materials, notify the Ministry of Public Security to locate the person sought. After the public security organ locates the person sought, it shall, depending on the circumstances, place the person sought under extradition detention or residential surveillance for extradition, and the Ministry of Public Security shall notify the Supreme People's Court. After the Supreme People's Court receives the notification from the Ministry of Public Security, it shall promptly transfer the extradition request and the attached documents and materials to the relevant Higher People's Court for examination.
If, after searching, the public security organ confirms that the person sought is not within the territory of the People's Republic of China or cannot be located, the Ministry of Public Security shall promptly notify the Supreme People's Court. After the Supreme People's Court receives the notification from the Ministry of Public Security, it shall promptly notify the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the search results, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall notify the requesting state.

Article 21 Where the Supreme People's Procuratorate, after examination, considers that the crime for which extradition is requested or other crimes of the person sought shall be prosecuted by the judicial organs of China, but no criminal proceedings have been initiated, it shall, within one month from the date of receiving the extradition request and the attached documents and materials, inform the Supreme People's Court and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of its intention to initiate criminal proceedings.

Article 22 The Higher People's Court shall examine the extradition request of the requesting state in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law and the extradition treaty on extradition conditions, and the examination shall be conducted by a collegiate panel composed of three judges.

Article 23 When examining an extradition case, the Higher People's Court shall hear the statements of the person sought and the opinions of a Chinese lawyer entrusted by the person sought. The Higher People's Court shall, within ten days from the date of receiving the extradition request forwarded by the Supreme People's Court, serve a copy of the extradition request on the person sought. The person sought shall submit his opinions within thirty days from the date of receipt.

Article 24 After examination, the Higher People's Court shall respectively make the following rulings:
(1) if it considers that the extradition request of the requesting state complies with the provisions of this Law and the extradition treaty, it shall make a ruling that the extradition conditions are met. If the person sought has a circumstance of deferred extradition as provided in Article 42 of this Law, the ruling shall state the same;
(2) if it considers that the extradition request of the requesting state does not comply with the provisions of this Law and the extradition treaty, it shall make a ruling of non-extradition.
At the request of the requesting state, and provided that it does not affect other ongoing proceedings within the territory of the People's Republic of China and does not infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of any third party within the territory of the People's Republic of China, a ruling may be made concurrently to transfer the property related to the case while making the ruling that extradition conditions are met.

Article 25 After the Higher People's Court makes a ruling that extradition conditions are met or a ruling of non-extradition, it shall pronounce the ruling to the person sought, and shall, within seven days from the date of making the ruling, submit the ruling and the relevant materials to the Supreme People's Court for review.
If the person sought disagrees with the ruling of the Higher People's Court that extradition conditions are met, the person sought and his entrusted Chinese lawyer may submit opinions to the Supreme People's Court within ten days from the date on which the People's Court pronounces the ruling to the person sought.

Article 27 In the process of examination, the People's Court may, when necessary, require the requesting state to provide supplementary materials within thirty days through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Article 28 After the Supreme People's Court makes a ruling approving or modifying, it shall, within seven days from the date of the ruling, deliver the written ruling to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and at the same time serve it on the person whose extradition is requested.
If the Supreme People's Court approves or makes a ruling of non-extradition, it shall immediately notify the public security organ to lift the compulsory measures taken against the person whose extradition is requested.

Article 29 After receiving the ruling of non-extradition from the Supreme People's Court, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall promptly notify the requesting state.
After receiving the ruling from the Supreme People's Court that the conditions for extradition are met, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall submit it to the State Council for a decision on whether to grant extradition.
If the State Council decides not to grant extradition, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall promptly notify the requesting state. The People's Court shall immediately notify the public security organ to lift the compulsory measures taken against the person whose extradition is requested.

Article 30 If, before a foreign state formally submits a request for extradition, an application is made due to urgent circumstances to take custody measures against the person whose extradition will be requested, the public security organ may, based on the application of the foreign state, take the measure of detention for extradition.
The application referred to in the preceding paragraph shall be submitted in writing through diplomatic channels or to the Ministry of Public Security, and shall specify:
(1) the contents prescribed in Articles 11 and 14 of this Law;
(2) a statement that the materials referred to in Article 12, paragraph (1) of this Law are already available; and
(3) a statement that a formal request for extradition will be formally submitted.
If the application is submitted through diplomatic channels, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall promptly forward the application to the Ministry of Public Security. If the application is submitted to the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Public Security shall notify the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the relevant information about the application.

Article 31 When the public security organ takes the measure of detention for extradition against the person whose extradition is requested in accordance with Article 30 of this Law, if the application was submitted to the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Public Security shall promptly notify the other party of the execution situation; if the application was submitted through diplomatic channels, the Ministry of Public Security shall notify the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the execution situation, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall promptly notify the requesting state. When notification is made through the aforementioned channels, if the person whose extradition is requested is already in detention for extradition, the time limit for submitting a formal request for extradition shall be notified at the same time.
If within thirty days after the public security organ takes the measure of detention for extradition, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has not received a formal request for extradition from the foreign state, the detention for extradition shall be revoked; upon request of that foreign state, the aforementioned time limit may be extended by fifteen days.
If the detention for extradition is revoked in accordance with paragraph 2 of this Article, the requesting state may subsequently formally submit a request for extradition of that person for the same offense.

Article 32 After the Higher People's Court receives the request for extradition and the attached documents and materials, if failure to take the measure of arrest for extradition may affect the normal progress of extradition, it shall promptly make a decision to arrest for extradition. If the measure of arrest for extradition is not taken against the person whose extradition is requested, it shall promptly make a decision to impose residential surveillance for extradition.
Article 33 The detention for extradition, arrest for extradition, and residential surveillance for extradition shall be executed by the public security organ.

Article 34 The organ that takes compulsory measures for extradition shall, within twenty-four hours after taking such compulsory measures for extradition, interrogate the person subjected to the compulsory measures for extradition.
A person subjected to compulsory measures for extradition may, from the date of being subjected to such measures, engage a Chinese lawyer to provide legal assistance. When executing compulsory measures for extradition, the public security organ shall inform the person subjected to the compulsory measures for extradition of the aforementioned rights.

Article 35 For a person whose extradition is requested who should be arrested for extradition, if he or she suffers from a serious disease, or is a pregnant woman or a woman nursing her own infant, the measure of residential surveillance for extradition may be taken.

Article 36 After the State Council makes a decision to grant extradition, it shall promptly notify the Supreme People's Court. If the person whose extradition is requested has not yet been arrested for extradition, the People's Court shall immediately decide to arrest for extradition.

Article 37 If a foreign state withdraws or abandons its request for extradition, the compulsory measures for extradition taken against the person whose extradition is requested shall be immediately lifted.

Article 38 The extradition shall be executed by the public security organ. If the State Council decides to grant extradition, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall promptly notify the Ministry of Public Security, and shall also notify the requesting state to agree with the Ministry of Public Security on the time, place, and manner of handing over the person whose extradition is requested, as well as other matters related to the execution of extradition.

Article 39 When extradition is executed in accordance with Article 38 of this Law, the public security organ shall, based on the ruling of the People's Court, hand over to the requesting state the property related to the case.
If the extradition cannot be executed due to the death, escape, or other reasons of the person whose extradition is requested, the aforementioned property may also be handed over to the requesting state.

Article 40 If the requesting state does not accept the person whose extradition is requested within fifteen days from the agreed date of handover, it shall be deemed to have voluntarily abandoned the extradition request. The public security organ shall immediately release the person whose extradition is requested, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs may no longer accept a request for extradition of that person for the same offense submitted again by that state.
If the requesting state cannot accept the person whose extradition is requested within the aforementioned time limit due to reasons beyond its control, it may apply for an extension of the time limit, but the extension shall not exceed thirty days, and it may also re-agree on the handover matters in accordance with Article 38 of this Law.

Article 41 If the extradited person escapes back to the People's Republic of China before the conclusion of criminal proceedings or completion of the service of sentence in the requesting state, a new extradition may be granted based on a repeated request for extradition for the same offense from the requesting state, without the requesting state being required to submit the documents and materials specified in Section 2 of this Chapter.

Article 42 When the State Council decides to grant extradition, if the judicial organs of the People's Republic of China are conducting criminal proceedings or executing a punishment against the person whose extradition is requested for another crime, it may simultaneously decide to defer extradition.

Article 43 If deferring extradition may cause serious obstacles to criminal proceedings in the requesting state, provided that it does not hinder the ongoing criminal proceedings within the territory of the People's Republic of China and the requesting state guarantees to immediately and unconditionally return the person whose extradition is requested after the completion of the relevant proceedings, the person may be temporarily extradited upon the request of the requesting state.
The decision on temporary extradition shall be made by the State Council after obtaining the consent of the Supreme People's Court or the Supreme People's Procuratorate.

Article 44 If extradition between foreign states requires transit through the territory of the People's Republic of China, a request for transit shall be submitted in accordance with Article 4 of this Law and the relevant provisions of Section 2 of this Chapter.
If transit is by air and there is no landing plan within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the preceding paragraph shall not apply; however, if an unscheduled landing occurs, a request for transit shall be submitted in accordance with the preceding paragraph.

Article 45 For a request for transit submitted by a foreign state, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Law, examine and make a decision to grant or refuse transit.
The decision to grant or refuse transit shall be notified by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to the requesting state through the same channel through which the request was received.
After the Ministry of Foreign Affairs makes a decision to grant transit, it shall promptly notify the Ministry of Public Security of that decision. Matters such as the time, place, and manner of transit shall be decided by the Ministry of Public Security.

Article 46 The transit for extradition shall be supervised or assisted in execution by the public security organ at the place of transit.
The public security organ may, upon the request of the state requesting transit, provide temporary custody facilities.

Article 47 Where a request is made to a foreign country for granting extradition or transit extradition, the adjudication, procuratorial, public security, state security or prison administration authorities of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government responsible for handling the relevant case shall submit opinions to the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security or the Ministry of Justice, respectively, together with relevant documents and materials and their certified translations. After the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security or the Ministry of Justice, together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, examine and approve the request, it shall be submitted to the foreign country through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Article 48 In an emergency, prior to making a formal request for extradition to a foreign country, a request may be made to the foreign country through diplomatic channels or other channels agreed by the requested country to take compulsory measures against the person concerned in advance.

Article 49 The instruments, documents and materials required for a request for extradition, transit extradition or taking compulsory measures shall be submitted in accordance with the provisions of the extradition treaty. If there is no extradition treaty or there are no provisions in the extradition treaty, the request may be submitted with reference to the provisions of Section 2, Section 4 and Section 7 of Chapter II of this Law. If the requested country has special requirements, the request may be submitted in accordance with the special requirements of the requested country, provided that the basic principles of the laws of the People's Republic of China are not violated.

Article 50 If the requested country attaches conditions to granting extradition, and the conditions do not impair the sovereignty, national interests or public interests of the People's Republic of China, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs may, on behalf of the Government of the People's Republic of China, make a commitment to the requested country. A commitment restricting prosecution shall be decided by the Supreme People's Procuratorate; a commitment regarding sentencing shall be decided by the Supreme People's Court.
When investigating criminal liability against the person extradited, the judicial authorities shall be bound by the commitment made.

Article 51 The public security organ shall be responsible for receiving the person extradited by the foreign country and the property relating to the case.
For extradition requests made by other departments, after receiving the person extradited and the property relating to the case, the public security organ shall promptly transfer them to the department that made the extradition request; it may also receive the person extradited and the property relating to the case together with the relevant departments.

Article 52 Where, in accordance with the provisions of this Law, the decision on whether to extradite is made by the State Council, the State Council may, when necessary, authorize the relevant departments of the State Council to make the decision.

Article 53 If after making a request, the requesting State withdraws or abandons the extradition request, or if the extradition request is erroneous and causes damage to the person sought for extradition, and the person sought for extradition claims compensation, the claim shall be made against the requesting State.

Article 54 Expenses incurred in handling extradition cases shall be handled in accordance with the extradition treaty or agreement jointly acceded to or concluded by the requesting State and the requested State.
Article 55 This Law shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
